blind_reader_rulings.reason: Both EN and AR source give only 'district — Hofuf' for these two cards, unlike the other eight which pair the district with a landmark (opposite Qasr Ibrahim, opposite King Faisal University, Prince Nawwaf Street, etc.). The pattern break is real but is inherited from the source data itself, not introduced by translation; the fence forbids inventing a landmark to smooth the pattern. Text stays faithful to source.

'Sharq Al-Qaisariyah' in the alt text is the EN source's own wording (pack.json en: "... of Sharq Al-Qaisariyah"), distinct on purpose from the venue's self-designated heading name 'Sharq Restaurant'. This exact split was reviewed and explicitly ruled correct by Eyad on 2026-09-04 (documented in the project CLAUDE.md: the restaurant sits in the historic Al-Hamidiyah souq building 'east of the Qaisariyah souq' — a valid positional description, not a naming conflict) and is called out as intentional in this batch's own BRIEF (trap 13). Unifying the two names would erase a source-sanctioned distinction.

'gekrönt von ihrem leuchtenden Schild' faithfully mirrors the EN source's own metaphor ('A modern glass façade crowned by its glowing sign' — pack.json en). It is a standing German image idiom (cf. 'ein Turm, gekrönt von einer Kuppel'), not an anglicism, and does not carry a quality/ranking claim (does not match the guarded terms beste/empfehlenswert/köstlich/lecker/berühmt). Flattening the register would diverge from the source's own stylistic choice without correcting an error.

The 'position in the list' framing is inherited directly from the source, not invented in translation: EN says 'the modern casual pick of the list', AR «الخيار العصري السريع في القائمة» ('in the list'). BRIEF trap 8 explicitly requires this card to read as a list-position description, not a recommendation, and bars beste/Empfehlung/Tipp. 'Eintrag' (entry) was deliberately chosen over 'Wahl' (choice) specifically to strip any evaluative connotation — softening the self-referential framing further risks tipping the sentence back toward an implied recommendation, which the fence forbids.

'Code' is the venue's own self-designated Latin name (name_en, BRIEF trap 10) and must stay verbatim and unflected per BINDING — it cannot be changed to avoid the momentary German-word misreading. The appositive '– Restaurant und Café –' was already inserted precisely to disambiguate on second reading; no further fix is available without violating the venue-name rule.

'so nennt es sich selbst' ('nennt sich' = 'is called') risks reading as if 'Restaurant und Café in einem' were the venue's official name, contradicting the heading 'Code'. EN source says 'as it calls itself' meaning a self-description of category, not a name-claim. 'so beschreibt sich der Ort selbst' preserves that exact meaning (self-description) while removing the name-collision risk — no fact added or removed.

'kündigen ... an' (ankündigen, plain 'announce') is an equally faithful, source-aligned rendering with a neutral register — no fact changed, only the verb's register.

notes:
Score 92/100 · APPROVE from the first loop. Six of thirty strings corrected at judge stage: dar-basma.alt and alhawi.blurb (pure reordering to fix PP-attachment/list-item ambiguity flagged by the blind reader, no fact touched), alkoot-hotel.alt (fixed a real missing-genitive-s error by switching to the batch's own established 'von <Name>' pattern), sinyar.blurb/sinyar.alt (Kalligraphie → Kalligrafie, Duden's current preferred spelling — judge catch, not from the blind reader), and koud.blurb (removed a name-collision risk in 'nennt sich' and lowered 'verkünden' to the more neutral, source-matching 'ankündigen'). Six of twelve blind-reader observations rejected: #1 is out of scope (page-frame text from de-din-1, not one of this batch's 30 keys); #4, #7, #10 would break sourced/BINDING decisions (Kulturerbe-Hotel term, the Sharq Al-Qaisariyah/Sharq Restaurant split ruled by Eyad 2026-09-04, and the unflected venue name 'Code'); #8 and #9 objected to register choices that are themselves faithful renderings of the EN/AR source's own wording, not translator overreach. One source_defect logged (#6: khunaina.area and sharq-alqaisariah.area lack a landmark because the EN/AR source itself gives none — not fabricatable).
BINDING: Alt-text strings on this page end WITHOUT a trailing full stop (10/10 in this batch, no exceptions) — keep this un-punctuated pattern for every restaurant single page (ج7).
BINDING: Use 'Kalligrafie' (Duden's current preferred de-DE spelling), not 'Kalligraphie', for calligraphy anywhere in German dining/restaurant content going forward.
BINDING: 'im traditionellen Stil' / 'traditionell' is the adjective for decorative heritage character (furniture, seating, décor, building style). 'Kulturerbe-' stays reserved exclusively for the one venue literally named 'Heritage Hotel' (Al-Koot Heritage Hotel & Restaurant) — never use 'Kulturerbe-' as a generic decorative adjective on ج7 pages.
BINDING: Self-designated venue names are never inflected. In alt texts use the plain labels «<Motiv> bei <Name>» / «<Motiv> von <Name>» (Dar Basma, Sinyar, Ammo, Lava, Code …); for the hotel the article-led genitive with the uninflected name, «des Al-Koot Heritage Hotel», as in the approved de-din-2 FAQ (coordinator override 2026-09-19).
BINDING: 'Sharq Al-Qaisariyah' (used in the alt text) and 'Sharq Restaurant' (the venue's self-designated heading name) are two source-sanctioned, deliberately distinct forms (Eyad's 2026-09-04 ruling, CLAUDE.md) — keep both as written on ج7, do not unify them.
BINDING: khunaina.area and sharq-alqaisariah.area intentionally carry no landmark (source gives none) — do not invent one on ج7 or elsewhere for these two venues.
